saints.name: St. Bonaventure
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The “Seraphic Doctor,” Franciscan Minister General and cardinal, who wed learning to love and wrote the classic ascent of the soul to God…
biography: Born at Bagnoregio in Tuscany about 1221, John of Fidanza — called Bonaventure — entered the Order of Friars Minor and studied at Paris alongside Thomas Aquinas. Elected Minister General of the Franciscans in 1257, he governed and reformed the order so wisely that he is often called its “second founder,” and he composed the standard life of St. Francis, the Legenda Maior.

He was named Cardinal Bishop of Albano and took a leading part in the Second Council of Lyons, which sought reunion with the Greek Church; he died during the council in 1274. His writings, above all The Journey of the Mind to God, unite theology and mysticism, earning him the title Doctor Seraphicus.
saints.knownFor: Uniting rigorous theology with Franciscan mysticism; reforming and shaping the Friars Minor.

canonization.canonized: 1482 by Pope Sixtus IV; declared a Doctor of the Church in 1588 by Pope Sixtus V

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 14 July
